topic: Find an equivalent fraction for 1/2 with denominator 8

fullData.title: Finding Equivalent Fractions on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Elementary Mathematics

problem.statement: Alex is baking a cake and needs to fill $\frac{1}{2}$ of a measuring cup. The cup is divided into $8$ equal parts. Use the number line to find out how many of those $8$ parts are equal to $\frac{1}{2}$.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Locate $\frac{1}{2}$ on the number line and find the matching eighths value at the same position.

rejections: In `content.visual`, the number line fails to mark position $0.5$ (or $\frac{1}{2}$). Although the grounding specifies locating the point $\frac{1}{2}$ at position $0.5$ and the alt text states the point is marked at the middle, the visual specifies `start: 0` and `jumps: []` with no point or jump landing at $0.5$.

steps.title: Locate one half on number line

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into 8 equal parts, with a clear point marked at the exact middle at 0.5, labeled as one half.

annotations.steps: I find the middle point between zero and one on the number line.
annotations.strategy: I notice that one-half is always right in the middle, exactly halfway between zero and one.
annotations.misconceptions: Read the scale first. Neighboring marks are not always one whole apart.
annotations.connections: This connects fractions to decimals and shows that one-half is a benchmark fraction used everywhere.
annotations.narrative: On the number line, locate the point $\frac{1}{2}$ at position $0.5$.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into 8 equal parts, with a jump highlighting the position at 4 out of 8 parts, which matches 1 half.

annotations.steps: I looked at the point where one half is marked and counted over to the eighths tick mark directly underneath it.
annotations.strategy: I notice that lining up different fraction pieces on the same scale helps me see which amounts are equal in size.
annotations.misconceptions: Start at the given number. Count the moves after it, not the starting mark.
annotations.connections: This connects the idea of equivalent fractions to decimals and percentages on the same number line.
annotations.narrative: At that same position $0.5$, the number line marks the point $\frac{4}{8}$. Therefore, $4$ of those $8$ parts are equal to $\frac{1}{2}$.

specs.title: Locate one half on number line
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Identify the benchmark fraction one-half as the exact midpoint between 0 and 1 on a number line.
specs.seedNotes: Render a number line from 0 to 1 highlighting the position 0.5 labeled with $\frac{1}{2}$.

specs.title: Identify the equivalent eighths mark
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Visualize fraction equivalence by observing how finer subdivisions align at the exact same position.
specs.seedNotes: Subdivide the number line into 8 equal parts and highlight that position 0.5 coincides with $\frac{4}{8}$, concluding that 4 parts are needed.

assignment.prompt: Before locating $\frac{1}{2}$, check the scale: what fraction does each single space between neighboring tick marks represent?
assignment.rationale: Because the distance from 0 to 1 is divided into 8 equal spaces, each space represents $\frac{1}{8}$, rather than 1 whole or $\frac{1}{7}$ from counting tick marks instead of intervals.
